EQUINE CARE

A preventive plan that fits the horse.

Management, travel, age and local disease risk help shape equine care. A thoughtful programme evolves with the horse rather than relying on a single universal schedule.

IN THIS GUIDE

Build prevention around exposureMonitor parasite controlKeep continuity between yard and clinic
All resources
01

Build prevention around exposure

Discuss the horse’s location, travel, contact with other horses and health history with the attending veterinarian. Vaccination choices depend on risk and the relevant product label. Professional guidance from another country provides background, not a universal schedule for local use.

02

Monitor parasite control

Faecal egg counts help characterise shedding, and faecal egg count reduction testing can help assess dewormer effectiveness. These tools support a broader veterinary programme; a count alone does not diagnose parasitic disease or establish the correct treatment.

03

Keep continuity between yard and clinic

A shared record of preventive care, medicines, changes in condition and follow-up appointments helps avoid gaps when horses move or receive care from more than one person. Confirm product authorisation and administration instructions for horses before use.
